messages.content: What is the freezing point point of water at a pressure of 10 kPa?

function.name: thermodynamics_calculate_boiling_point

message.content:
At a pressure of **10 kPa** (≈ 0.099 atm), pure water freezes at roughly **+2 °C**.  

This follows from the negative slope of the ice–water melting line: as pressure drops below atmospheric levels, the equilibrium temperature between ice and liquid rises slightly above 0 °C. At 10 kPa the shift is modest—about two degrees warmer than the standard 0 °C freezing point at 1 atm.
